recapture_recommended.detail: Every capture is 1024 px wide and has been through WhatsApp recompression. Full-screen on a 1080p timeline that is a 1.9x upscale, and any panel zoom is a 3-4x upscale, which will visibly smear the panel text. Recapture at native display resolution (1920 px or wider) with a lossless PNG path if these are to fill the frame.

The set proves the lock errors numerically (3,158 in the counter and the by-phase chart) but the message text is never legible: the correlated-logs panel shows empty body cells, an empty exception.message column for the visible rows, and the traceforge.phase column clipped at the right edge. Recapture the correlated-logs panel widened or expanded on an error row so the message reads on screen.
The visible rows all show status Unset at ~100 ms, so the table does not show the failing spans. Sort or filter that panel by error status before recapturing.

Durations render as raw nanoseconds (69,049,363,160) and the table mixes workflow stages with FastAPI routes such as GET /api/v1/runs. It is also not filtered by phase, so it repeats identically across all three phase captures. Format the column as duration and filter to workflow spans before recapturing.

The three *-05 captures are near-duplicates showing two 'No Data' panels. Zero failures is the right result, but it does not read as a result. Either replace with a panel that renders an explicit zero, or drop these frames.
The by-phase graphs are a single hairline spike on a 24-hour axis, so the shape carries no information. Narrow the dashboard time range to the run window before recapturing.

accuracy_warnings: Do not caption 'Requests observed server-side' as the k6 request count. It counts spans in the phase window: 5,522 / 3,522 / 5,633 on screen against 5,524 / 6,499 / 5,637 client requests. The candidate gap is large because many failing requests never produced a completed server span.

Do not caption the candidate as '94.4% errors' from these images. The panels support 3,158 error spans out of 3,522, which is 89.7% server-side. The 94.40% figure is the k6 client-side failure rate from the same run and belongs to a different frame.
The stage-duration and MCP panels are run-wide, not phase-scoped. Do not imply the numbers change between the baseline, candidate, and patched captures; they do not.
